tables.source_file: plsql/packages/PKG_SECURITY.pkb (referenced; DDL not found in Tables.sql deep scan)
tables.extraction_note: Table DDL not present in recovered schema files. Structure inferred entirely from PKG_SECURITY package body references and comments. Marked INFERRED.
tables.comment: Stores per-employee authentication credentials. Separate from EMPLOYEES to isolate credential data. Referenced by PKG_SECURITY.authenticate and PKG_SECURITY.change_password.

columns.name: PASSWORD_HASH
columns.notes: MD5 hash of password; produced by PKG_SECURITY.hash_password using DBMS_CRYPTO.HASH_MD5 → RAWTOHEX

missing_columns_noted: LOGIN_ATTEMPTS — no failed-attempt counter; brute-force lockout impossible (DQ-023)
LAST_LOGIN — not tracked here; partial record exists in USER_SESSIONS
security_findings: CRITICAL: PASSWORD_HASH uses MD5 (DBMS_CRYPTO.HASH_MD5). MD5 is cryptographically broken for password storage — rainbow tables and pre-image attacks exist. Should be PBKDF2/bcrypt (DQ-010).
CRITICAL: PKG_SECURITY.authenticate does not query USER_CREDENTIALS to verify the supplied password. Authentication is effectively bypassed — any password is accepted for a valid username (DQ-003).
HIGH: No failed-attempt counter. Unlimited brute-force login attempts are possible against PKG_SECURITY.authenticate (DQ-023).
VULNERABILITY: Timing attack — authenticate() raises different exceptions for unknown username vs wrong password, allowing username enumeration.

NOTE: PKG_SECURITY.change_password calls PKG_AUDIT.log_action('USER_CREDENTIALS', p_emp_id, 'UPDATE', USER) but the actual UPDATE DML is marked as a stub ('NOTE: Actual password update would go to USER_CREDENTIALS table — This is a stub for the legacy system model').

HIGH: PKG_SECURITY.change_password accepts p_old_password parameter but never verifies it against the stored hash. Any authenticated session can overwrite any employee credential without knowing the current password (DQ-029, BR-044).
HIGH: If two ACTIVE employees share the same EMAIL, PKG_SECURITY.authenticate silently resolves to MIN(EMP_ID) via TOO_MANY_ROWS handler — second employee cannot log in as themselves (BR-043b).

MEDIUM: PKG_SECURITY package spec declares e_account_locked (ORA-20302) and e_session_expired (ORA-20303) as named exceptions but neither is raised anywhere in the package body. Callers catching these exceptions will never fire (DQ-030, BR-045).
password_complexity_rules: Must contain at least one uppercase letter A-Z (ORA-20311)
Must contain at least one digit 0-9 (ORA-20312)
Enforced by PKG_SECURITY.change_password; NOT enforced at DDL level
tables.audit_integration: PKG_AUDIT.log_action called on credential UPDATE with table name 'USER_CREDENTIALS', record_id = EMP_ID, action = 'UPDATE', username = built-in USER
